issues.title: sanitizeLabel's dash-boundary cut collapses a long label to its first word, re-introducing session-name and SlugHint collisions
issues.description: cli/internal/launch/launch.go:684-698. The FR1.4 cap cuts on the LAST '-' inside s[:48] with no floor on what survives, so any title whose first 48 sanitized bytes contain only an early dash collapses to that first segment. Measured against the shipped code: "A supercalifragilisticexpialidociousreallylongidentifiername" -> "a" (1 byte); "x abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" -> "x"; "Refactor NotificationDeliveryOrchestrationPipelineForRealtimeEvents" -> "refactor". This is a realistic title shape (a verb plus one long CamelCase identifier), and it defeats FR1.4's own stated goal ("48 keeps them readable and still unique"). Consequences: (a) two plans whose titles share a first word both mint session base `gogo-plan-refactor`, so uniqueSession starts appending -2/-3 and SessionMatchesSlug can no longer tell them apart - the same attribution ambiguity coding-rules.md TEST-005 exists to prevent, arriving through a lossy transform instead of a substring match; (b) plans_tab.go:47 planSlugHint now runs the same transform, so the member SlugHint shown in the plan detail and written into the project changelog degrades to "a"/"refactor" too. Before this change both names were fully distinct. TestSanitizeLabelBounded does not catch it: its boundary assertion ("the last segment must be a whole word of the original") passes for every degenerate case above.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. In sanitizeLabel, only honour the '-' boundary when the cut keeps a useful prefix, else hard-cut: replace `if i := strings.LastIndex(s, "-"); i > 0` with `if i := strings.LastIndex(s, "-"); i > MaxSessionLabel/2` (or any floor >= ~24). The hard-cut branch already exists and is already tested (the one-word case). Extend TestSanitizeLabelBounded with the degenerate fixtures: assert `len(sanitizeLabel("A " + strings.Repeat("z", 60))) >= MaxSessionLabel/2` and that two titles differing only after the first word yield DIFFERENT sanitized labels.
issues.fix_summary:
Added the floor: the '-' boundary is honoured only when it survives past MaxSessionLabel/2 (24), else the hard cut stands. Extended TestSanitizeLabelBounded with the three degenerate fixtures plus the property that matters - two titles sharing only a first word must yield DIFFERENT labels and must not cross-attribute via SessionMatchesSlug. Mutation-verified: restoring `i > 0` fails the test.

[review round 02] Round 02 re-verified independently. Read the shipped floor (`i > MaxSessionLabel/2`) and re-ran the degenerate fixtures: "Refactor Notification..." now hard-cuts to a 48-byte label instead of collapsing to "refactor", and two titles sharing only a first word stay distinct. Own mutation (floor -> `i > 0`) fails TestSanitizeLabelBounded. Cross-checked end-to-end in the HEAD-vs-shipped argv dump: the two degenerate titles are the ONLY session names that differ, and both differ by the specified 48-byte cap with no trailing dash.

issues.title: FoldToPointer is wired only into the TUI: `gogo plan go` / `gogo plan promote` still build a 20 951-byte command and now hard-fail at the new preflight
issues.description: cli/plan.go:444 (planGo fan-out) and cli/plan.go:559 (planPromote) build the IDENTICAL over-budget intent as the plans tab - `launch.PlanIntent(p.Title, goal, p.ID)` with `goal = plans.BriefFor(p, target)` - and hand it straight to `planLauncher` with no `launch.FoldToPointer` call. Measured against the shipped code with the user's real shape (a ~20 KB per-source brief, plan `plan-30939c06`): the CLI path builds a 20 951-byte command line (limit 16 317) while the plans-tab path folds the same input to 275 bytes. So after this release the reported bug is fixed behind `m`/`c` in the cockpit but is still fully live behind `gogo plan go` - which README.md itself advertises as the scriptable equivalent ("`gogo plan go` fans out the spawn"). The new preflight does improve the message there (a typed CommandTooLongError naming the byte count instead of `exit status 1`), but the user is still blocked on a limit they did not create - exactly the outcome D1 rejected as option B. Note the scope caveat: plan.md's Changes checklist scopes the fold to the three TUI sites and does not list cli/plan.go, so this is a gap in the plan's coverage rather than a deviation from it - but FR1.3 is phrased as a property of the launch, not of a key binding.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE (2 lines, one per site, same shape as plans_tab.go:707). At cli/plan.go:444 add `intent.Root = src.Path` then `intent = launch.FoldToPointer(intent, plans.Path(project, p.ID), target)` AFTER the existing `intent.Command += launch.SkipParams(...)`; at cli/plan.go:559 add `intent.Root = src.Path` then `intent = launch.FoldToPointer(intent, plans.Path(project, p.ID), sname)`. Cover it with a plan.go test using the injected `planLauncher` seam: assert the captured intent's command is under `launch.MaxTmuxCommandBytes` and carries `plans.Path(project, id)`. If the reviewer's scope call is to keep this release strictly TUI-only, downgrade to `wontfix` and record it in decisions.md as the follow-up - but do not ship it silently.
issues.fix_summary:
Wired the same FoldToPointer seam at both headless doors - cli/plan.go planGo (intent.Root = src.Path; FoldToPointer(intent, plans.Path(project, p.ID), target), after SkipParams so the params survive) and planPromote (same, section = sname). Added plan_fold_test.go: TestCmdPlanGoFoldsOversizedBrief and TestCmdPlanPromoteFoldsOversizedBrief drive the real cmdPlanStore through the injected planLauncher and assert the captured command is under MaxTmuxCommandBytes and carries plans.Path; TestCmdPlanDoorsUnderBudgetAreByteForByte pins the no-op. Mutation-verified: deleting either fold line fails its test.

[review round 02] Round 02 re-verified independently, by my own method rather than the developer's test. Compiled the HEAD (0.27.0) cli module and the shipped one side by side, drove the REAL cli/plan.go doors (planGo fan-out + planPromote) through the injected planLauncher over 8 under-budget plans (24 launches: punctuation, newlines, shell metacharacters, unicode, trailing dashes, both degenerate titles) and diffed the produced argv. The launched COMMAND element is byte-identical in 24/24 - the only delta anywhere is the `-s` session NAME on the two >48-char titles (FR1.4's cap). Own mutations deleting either fold line fail their own test. Section arguments checked: planGo passes `target` (the same key BriefFor was just called with) and planPromote passes `sname` (sourceInProject's canonical source NAME, which is what a `### <name>` heading uses - correct even when the user passed a path), matching the TUI's semantics.

issues.title: TestAttachFailureIsReported asserts a test-local copy of the callback, not the production code - FR1.6 is untested at both attach sites
issues.description: cli/internal/tui/plans_view_test.go:471-502. The test calls `m.attachSession(...)` only to check the returned cmd is non-nil, then asserts against `attachOutcome`, a helper DEFINED IN THE TEST FILE (line 497) that re-implements the decision the production closures make. Mutation-verified: deleting the `if err != nil { return launchDoneMsg{... level: statusLevelErr} }` branch from update.go:623-626 (i.e. reverting FR1.6 exactly) leaves `go test ./internal/tui/` fully GREEN. The same holds for peek.go:114-117. So the one FR whose whole point is "the error must no longer be discarded" has no regression guard, and the test's own comment ("mirrors the attach callback's decision so both attach sites are asserted") claims coverage it does not provide - the shape code-review-standards.md #8 warns about.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Extract the callback body into a package-level function in update.go, e.g. `func attachOutcome(session string, err error) launchDoneMsg`, and have BOTH `attachSession` (update.go) and `attachFromPeek` (peek.go) pass it to `tea.ExecProcess` (`func(err error) tea.Msg { return attachOutcome(session, err) }`). Delete the duplicate from plans_view_test.go so the existing table drives the real function. Re-run the mutation to confirm the test now fails when the `if err != nil` branch is removed.
issues.fix_summary:
Extracted the decision into a package-level tui.attachOutcome(session, err) in update.go; BOTH attachSession and peek.go's attachFromPeek now pass it to tea.ExecProcess. Deleted the test-local duplicate so TestAttachFailureIsReported drives the production function, and added TestAttachSitesShareOneOutcome, which reads the two sources and fails if either rebuilds the status inline (so a future copy cannot escape the guard). Mutation-verified: deleting the `if err != nil` branch now fails the suite (it was green before).

[review round 02] Round 02 re-verified independently. attachOutcome is now a package-level function in update.go and BOTH sites (attachSession, peek.go attachFromPeek) pass it to tea.ExecProcess; the test-local duplicate is gone. Three own mutations all bite where the round-01 equivalent was green: deleting the `if err != nil` branch fails TestAttachFailureIsReported, and re-inlining the closure at EITHER site fails the new TestAttachSitesShareOneOutcome. The blind spot is genuinely closed, not re-asserted.

issues.title: planKebab (the CLI mirror of planSlugHint) was left on the old regex, so the two doors into plans.AddMember now write different SlugHints
issues.description: cli/plan.go:657-666 still uses `planKebabUnsafe = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-z0-9]+`)` with no length bound, while cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:47 was moved onto `launch.SlugFromLabel`. Both write the SAME field of the SAME store: `plans.AddMember(project, id, plans.Member{Source: sname, SlugHint: planKebab(p.Title)})` (plan.go:453, plan.go:566) vs `plans.Member{Source: sourceName, SlugHint: planSlugHint(p.Title)}` (plans_tab.go:525, :730). For the title "Catalogue side - normalise" the CLI now writes `catalogue-side-normalise` and the TUI writes `catalogue-side---normalise`; for any 48+ char title the CLI writes the full slug and the TUI writes the capped one. The hint is rendered in the plan detail ("slug:<hint>"), in `MembersShippedIn`'s unshipped list (internal/plans/plans.go:563) and in the project changelog line (plans.go:685), so the same plan reads differently depending on which door spawned it. Before this change the two transforms were identical - this release introduced the drift, which is exactly what coding-rules.md "Keep enumerations in sync" and code-review-standards.md #1 forbid. Not a correctness bug: the spawn guards (`planHasMember`, `targetSpawned`) key on Source alone, so no duplicate member is created.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Replace planKebab's body with the same delegation the TUI uses: `func planKebab(title string) string { if strings.TrimSpace(title) == "" { return "plan" }; return launch.SlugFromLabel(title) }`, drop the now-unused `planKebabUnsafe` var, and add a one-line assertion (in plan_test.go or the launch test) that `planKebab(x) == planSlugHint(x)` for a title containing " - " and for a 60-char title.
issues.fix_summary:
planKebab now delegates to launch.SlugFromLabel - the same transform the session name and the TUI's planSlugHint use - keeping only the CLI's own blank-title 'plan' fallback; the planKebabUnsafe regexp and the now-unused regexp import are gone. Added TestPlanKebabMatchesTUITransform asserting planKebab == launch.SlugFromLabel over the two shapes that had drifted (' - ' and 48+ chars) plus the attribution property. Mutation-verified: any divergent body fails the test.

[review round 02] Round 02 re-verified independently. Grepped the whole module: exactly ONE label transform survives (launch.go sessionUnsafe); both doors delegate to launch.SlugFromLabel (plan.go:678, plans_tab.go:51) and no third copy exists (the other regexes are the CLI slug validator, the plan-id sanitizer and a diagram helper - unrelated). Own mutation restoring the old planKebab regex fails TestPlanKebabMatchesTUITransform.

issues.title: Three shipped wirings have no test that bites: planSlugHint's alignment and the fold at the `c` and `A` call sites
issues.description: Mutation-verified against the shipped tree (each mutation applied alone, then `go test ./internal/...`): (1) reverting cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:47 planSlugHint to the old `[^a-z0-9]+` regex - i.e. undoing the second half of FR1.7 - leaves every test GREEN; (2) deleting the `intent = launch.FoldToPointer(intent, m.planPath(p.ID), sourceName)` line at plans_tab.go:522 (the `c` create-work-item site) leaves every test GREEN; (3) deleting `intent = launch.FoldToPointer(intent, planPath, "")` at plans_tab.go:963 (the `A` plan-with-claude site) leaves every test GREEN. plan.md's Changes checklist names all three explicitly ("Align planSlugHint with sanitizeLabel"; "Fold-to-pointer at the two spawn sites and in finishPlanWithClaude"), and TestSpawnOversizedBriefFoldsToPointer covers only the `m` fan-out site. TestFoldToPointerFoldsAnAuthoringGoal exercises the launch-package function, not the TUI wiring that calls it.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add three cheap assertions to plans_view_test.go: (a) `TestPlanSlugHintMatchesSessionTransform` - for a title containing " - ", assert `planSlugHint(title) == launch.SlugFromLabel(title)` and that `launch.SessionMatchesSlug(<the session the spawn would mint>, planSlugHint(title))` is true; (b) extend TestSpawnOversizedBriefFoldsToPointer with a `c`-key variant (open the detail, press `c` on the source row) asserting the captured intent is under MaxTmuxCommandBytes; (c) an `A`-key variant driving finishPlanWithClaude with a >16 KB goal and asserting the captured intent carries `plans.Path(...)` and no inlined goal.
issues.fix_summary:
Added three biting tests to plans_view_test.go: TestPlanSlugHintMatchesSessionTransform (hint == launch.SlugFromLabel, and the minted session attributes back to the recorded hint), TestCreateWorkItemFoldsOversizedBrief (drives the real `c` key through Update and asserts the captured intent is under the limit and points at the plan file), and TestPlanWithClaudeFoldsOversizedGoal (drives finishPlanWithClaude with a ~24 KB goal, asserts the fold, that the gogo-project-plan skill instruction SURVIVES it, and that the goal is preserved in the plan file the pointer names). Mutation-verified: each of the three reverts named in the issue now fails.

[review round 02] Round 02 re-verified independently. All three previously-blind reverts now bite under my own harness: planSlugHint -> old regex fails TestPlanSlugHintMatchesSessionTransform; deleting the fold at the `c` site fails TestCreateWorkItemFoldsOversizedBrief; deleting it at the `A` site fails TestPlanWithClaudeFoldsOversizedGoal. Round 01's exact three green-on-revert cases are gone.

issues.title: FR3.2's "every outcome is classified" is incomplete: four refusal/failure status sites still render as plain dim success
issues.description: The severity plumbing is correct and well tested, but four outcome sites were missed, and one of them sits in the SAME `if` as a classified sibling: (1) cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:402 `m.status = fmt.Sprintf("refusing - %d of %d member(s) not shipped: %s", ...)` - the branch two lines above it (`len(p.Members) == 0`) DID get `statusBlocked`, so the identical project-UAT refusal renders amber or dim depending on which arm fires; (2) plans_tab.go:456 the same refusal inside finishPlanDone; (3) cli/internal/tui/update.go:157-165, the planAuthorLaunchedMsg headless branch ("no tmux - the analyst is running headless in the background ... `tmux` recommended") - a degraded fallback the user should notice, rendered as a success; (4) update.go:808-810 `m.status = "killed N session(s)"` + `", M failed"` - a partial kill failure now has tmux's own words available through the new TmuxError and discards both the words and the severity. plan.md's outcome-taxonomy diagram puts (1)-(3) squarely in the `Blocked` state and (4) in `Failed`. Secondary note on discipline: statusLevel is reset only at Update's tea.KeyMsg choke point, so (3) and `attachSession`'s bare `m.status = "attaching " + session` (update.go:620) inherit whatever level the previous async message left; I could not construct a concrete sequence where a stale error level survives to colour them, but classifying them removes the question.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Wrap the four sites: plans_tab.go:402 and :456 -> `m.statusBlocked(fmt.Sprintf(...))`; update.go:165 -> `m.statusBlocked(status)`; update.go:808-810 -> build the string first, then `m.statusFailed(s)` when `failed > 0` else `m.setStatus(statusLevelOK, s)`, and carry the first killer error's `err.Error()` the way finishPlanSpawn now carries firstErr. Add `m.setStatus(statusLevelOK, "attaching " + session)` at update.go:620. Extend TestStatusSeverityDistinguishesOutcomes with the project-UAT refusal so the taxonomy is guarded rather than sampled.
issues.fix_summary:
Classified all four: the two project-UAT refusals (plans_tab.go planAcceptUAT's second arm and finishPlanDone's re-guard) -> statusBlocked, matching their already-blocked sibling; the planAuthorLaunchedMsg headless branch -> statusBlocked (a degraded fallback the user should notice); and finishKill's partial failure -> statusFailed carrying the FIRST killer error's own words (now tmux's, via TmuxError) instead of a bare count, with a clean kill still on the dim voice. attachSession's 'attaching <session>' now goes through setStatus(statusLevelOK, ...) so it cannot inherit a stale async level. Added TestProjectUATRefusalIsBlocked (both arms) and TestPartialKillFailureIsReported (failure AND clean paths, with a View() assertion).

[review round 02] Round 02: the reported defect is resolved - all four sites are classified in the code (plans_tab.go:404 and :458 -> statusBlocked, update.go:167 headless-analyst -> statusBlocked, update.go:828 finishKill -> statusFailed carrying the first killer error's words), plus attachSession's setStatus(statusLevelOK, ...). finishKill verified by driving the REAL function on four paths: clean 2 -> "killed 2 sessions" and clean 1 -> "killed 1 session" at level OK with no marker (byte-for-byte preserved); partial -> "killed 1 session, 1 failed: tmux kill-session failed: exit status 1: can't find session: gogo-go-b" at level Err rendering the error marker; total failure likewise. Closing as verified. The residual TEST-coverage gap around three of these sites is raised separately as REV-011.

issues.title: `M` with a ready selection shows "FORCING past the source cap" on a merged-ship confirm that never consulted the cap
issues.description: cli/internal/tui/move.go:193-199. launchActionForce computes `override := m.capBounce(m.focusedCard())` unconditionally, but attemptActionForce returns the merged-ship intent from the SELECTION branch (move.go:42-61) before any capBounce is reached - the cap guard only exists on the ClassUnfinished / ClassInProgress arms. So when a ready card is selected and the cursor happens to rest on a cap-blocked card, `M` opens a `/gogo:done` confirm whose description falsely claims to be forcing past a cap. Reproduced against the shipped tree with a three-card fixture (busy in-progress + live session, next unfinished, shipme ready; cap 1): the rendered confirm reads `will run: claude "/gogo:done shipme" ...` on one line and `FORCING past the source cap - cap 1 reached in web - already building busy (th...` on the next. A confirm dialog is the safety surface for a state-changing launch, so wrong text there is worse than merely cosmetic.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Only compute the override note when the resolved action is actually the one the cap guards. Simplest correct form: move the capture after the guard call and gate it on the intent, e.g. compute `intent, isShip, bounce := m.attemptActionForce(ship, force)` first, then `if force && !isShip && len(m.selectedFeatures()) == 0 { override = m.capBounce(m.focusedCard()) }` - capBounce is a pure read, so calling it after the guard changes nothing. Extend TestForceMoveOverridesCap with a selection case asserting the ship confirm carries NO "FORCING past the source cap" text.
issues.fix_summary:
The override note is now computed AFTER the guard and only when the resolved action is the one the cap guards: `if force && !isShip && len(m.selectedFeatures()) == 0`. capBounce is a pure read, so moving it changes nothing else. Added TestForceMoveOnSelectionClaimsNoOverride reproducing the reviewer's three-card fixture (ready selected, cursor on the cap-blocked card) and asserting the /gogo:done confirm carries NO force wording; the existing TestForceMoveOverridesCap still pins that a genuine override DOES say so. Mutation-verified: restoring the unconditional form fails the new test.

[review round 02] Round 02 re-verified independently for the reported scope. The override note is now computed after the guard and gated on `force && !isShip && len(m.selectedFeatures()) == 0`; my own reproduction of the round-01 three-card fixture (ready card selected, cursor on the cap-blocked card) now shows a clean /gogo:done confirm with no force wording, and my mutation restoring the unconditional form fails TestForceMoveOnSelectionClaimsNoOverride. TestForceMoveOverridesCap still pins that a genuine override DOES say so. The selection arm is closed; a second arm of the same class (accept) is raised separately as REV-010.

issues.title: AttachArgs is the one tmux `-t` target left on prefix/fnmatch resolution
issues.description: cli/internal/launch/launch.go:844-849. `AttachArgs` still emits `switch-client -t <session>` / `attach-session -t <session>` while has-session, kill-session and capture-pane all moved to the exact form this release added. Both take a target-session, so they are subject to the same exact -> prefix -> fnmatch resolution plan.md measured and called "a wrong-session hazard". The window is narrow - every caller (`attachSession`, `attachFromPeek`, `attachFeature`) passes a name that came from `launch.ListSessions()` or a fresh `Result.Session`, so an exact match normally exists and wins - but if that session exits between the listing and the attach, tmux falls back to a prefix match and drops the user INTO A DIFFERENT feature's live session, which is the worst place for this class of bug to land. Raised as a nit, not a defect, because FR1.5 named only the three probes and the fix wants the same live verification A2 got.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, but verify before shipping. Change AttachArgs to use the exact SESSION form (`exactTarget(session)`, i.e. `=<name>` - NOT the pane form) for both branches, then confirm live on tmux 3.7b that `attach-session -t "=<name>"` and `switch-client -t "=<name>"` both work and both refuse a prefix, exactly as A2 did for capture-pane. Pin it with an argv assertion in launch_test.go's AttachArgs test. If the live check shows either subcommand rejects the `=` form, close this as wontfix with the measurement recorded in adjustments.md.
issues.fix_summary:
Verified live on tmux 3.7b FIRST, both branches, before changing anything: `attach-session -t '=<exact>'` attaches and `-t '=<prefix>'` is refused; `switch-client -t '=<exact>'` returns rc=0 and moves the client, `-t '=<prefix>'` is refused, and a BARE prefix resolved to a different session (the hazard, reproduced). switch-client needed a control-mode client (`tmux -C attach`, addressed by #{client_name}) to test safely - the host's only real client is the user's live session and was never touched. AttachArgs now uses exactTarget(session) - the bare '=' SESSION form, never the pane form's trailing ':' - on both branches; TestAttachArgs pins both argv shapes and asserts no trailing colon leaks in. Mutation-verified: reverting either branch fails the test.

[review round 02] Round 02 re-verified independently. Read the shipped AttachArgs: both branches emit exactTarget(session) - the bare `=<name>` SESSION form - and neither carries the pane form's trailing `:`; TestAttachArgs pins both argv shapes plus the no-trailing-colon property, and my own mutations reverting EITHER branch fail it. Live-session safety confirmed separately: `tmux list-sessions` (read-only) shows the user's two sessions intact, and no test in the module calls launch.Launch / launch.KillSession / execs tmux - every launcher and killer path goes through an injected seam, so nothing in the suite can address, attach to or kill them.

issues.title: A pre-0.28.0 live session whose label exceeds 48 chars loses its board attribution after the upgrade
issues.description: FR1.4's cap changes the SLUG side of the comparison as well as the name side, so `SessionMatchesSlug` stops matching sessions that were minted by 0.27.0 with an uncapped label. Verified against the user's ACTUAL running session on this host (read-only `tmux list-sessions`): `gogo-plan-catalogue-side-of-the-matching-engine---normalise-store-embed-hard-filter` (83 chars). Under the shipped code, `sanitizeLabel("Catalogue side of the matching engine - normalise, store, embed, hard-filter")` = `catalogue-side-of-the-matching-engine`, so 0.28.0 would mint `gogo-plan-catalogue-side-of-the-matching-engine` and `SessionMatchesSlug(<the live 83-char session>, <its title>)` returns FALSE. Consequences for that already-running session the moment the user upgrades: no live ● dot, `a` reports "no running session", `l` falls back to the log, and the per-source cap under-counts it - exactly the degradation FR1.7 exists to remove, arriving as an upgrade-transition effect. The host's other live session (`gogo-author-for-gogo-project-lets-add-few-new-tasks-to-plan`, a 46-char label) is unaffected and still matches. Self-healing: it affects only sessions started before the upgrade, and only those past the cap; anything relaunched under 0.28.0 attributes normally. Notable because the one affected session is the plan this very feature was built for.
issues.proposed_solution: NEEDS-USER-DECISION on whether to absorb it, then AGENT-FIXABLE either way. Option A (recommended, ~6 lines, no contract change): make SessionMatchesSlug ALSO accept the pre-cap form - compute `uncapped := strings.Trim(sessionUnsafe.ReplaceAllString(strings.ToLower(slug), "-"), "-")` alongside the capped `sanitized` and test the session against both bases (plus the numeric collision suffix). It is a strict widening of an exact-boundary match, so TEST-005's non-matches are untouched; pin it with a case asserting the real 83-char session attributes to its title. Option B (zero code): accept the transition and note it in the release changelog - 'sessions started before 0.28.0 with a >48-char label show no live dot until relaunched'. Option C: leave as-is silently - not recommended, since the user will see it on their own running session.
issues.fix_summary: Widened SessionMatchesSlug to match against BOTH label transforms: the bounded one 0.28.0 mints with and the pre-0.28.0 unbounded one (new unexported unboundedLabel; sanitizeLabel is now that plus the cap, so there is one reduction and the bound is a separate step). Read-side only - sessionName/minting stays bounded, so FR1.4 is not relaxed and no new long name is ever created. It cannot reintroduce REV-001's ambiguity because each candidate is still compared as a WHOLE base (exact, or base + a purely-numeric suffix), so a second candidate can never turn a prefix into a match. TestSessionMatchesSlugSurvivesTheUpgrade uses the host's two REAL running session names as fixtures (the 83-char gogo-plan-catalogue-... and the 59-char gogo-author-...), asserts the freshly-minted bounded name still matches, that the legacy base accepts the collision suffix, that minting stays under the cap, and includes 7 non-match cases (a shorter sibling title, prefixes, and TEST-005's originals) proving the widening cross-attributes nothing. Verified live read-only against the running host: both real sessions now report matches=true.

issues.title: REV-007's fix closed the selection arm only: `M` on a plan-pending card still claims to force past a cap the accept arm never consulted
issues.description: cli/internal/tui/move.go:255-258. The new gate is `if force && !isShip && len(m.selectedFeatures()) == 0`, which correctly excludes the merged-ship path REV-007 reported - but `attemptActionForce`'s ClassUnfinished arm returns the ACCEPT intent at move.go:83-85 BEFORE any capBounce is reached (the code's own comment says "Accept is uncapped (it doesn't drive build work)"), and an accept has isShip=false and needs no selection, so it sails through the new gate. Reproduced against the shipped tree with a two-card fixture (busy in-progress + live session, pending at `awaiting-plan-acceptance`, cap 1, cursor on `pending`): pressing `M` renders `will run: claude "/gogo:accept pending"` on one line and `FORCING past the source cap - cap 1 reached in web - already building busy (th...` on the next. Same class and same severity as REV-007 - wrong text on the confirm dialog, which is the safety surface for a state-changing launch - on a different arm. Raised as a new id rather than reopening REV-007 because REV-007's reported scope (the selection branch) is genuinely closed and independently verified.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, and the general form is simpler than the current clause: ask the guard itself what the force actually overrode, instead of enumerating the arms that do not consult the cap. Replace the gate with `if force { if _, _, b := m.attemptActionForce(ship, false); b != "" { override = b } }`, placed where it is now (after the forced call's own bounce early-return, so an illegal move still exits first). attemptActionForce is a pure read, so the extra call costs nothing and is correct for EVERY arm - selection, accept, ready-to-ship and shipped - by construction, with no list to keep in sync. Extend TestForceMoveOnSelectionClaimsNoOverride into a table covering the accept arm and a ready card as well.
issues.fix_summary: Replaced the arm-enumerating gate with the guard-derived one the reviewer proposed: `if force { if _, _, unforced := m.attemptActionForce(ship, false); unforced != "" { override = unforced } }`, placed after the forced call's own bounce early-return. Re-running the guard UNFORCED yields exactly the bounce the force suppressed - "" for every arm that never consults the cap - so it is correct for selection, accept, ready and shipped by construction, with no list to keep in sync. attemptActionForce is a pure read. TestForceMoveOnSelectionClaimsNoOverride became the 4-case table TestForceMoveClaimsOverrideOnlyWhenItOverrode (go / accept / ready-selection / ready-focused), asserting the force wording appears ONLY on the go arm and that when it does it names the real cap.

issues.title: Three of REV-006's four classifications are unguarded, and TestProjectUATRefusalIsBlocked's "other arm" block silently re-tests the arm it already covered
issues.description: The REV-006 code fix is correct, but its test does not hold three quarters of it. Own mutation harness (each revert applied alone, compile-checked first, then `go test ./...`): reverting `m.statusBlocked(...)` to a bare `m.status = ...` at plans_tab.go:398 (planAcceptUAT's NO-MEMBERS arm), at plans_tab.go:458 (finishPlanDone's re-guard) or at update.go:167 (the headless-analyst branch) leaves the ENTIRE suite green; so does reverting attachSession's `setStatus(statusLevelOK, ...)`. Only the second planAcceptUAT arm and finishKill actually bite. The cause of the no-members gap is a fixture bug: TestProjectUATRefusalIsBlocked's second block is commented "The OTHER arm (no members at all) must agree", but it reuses the same seeded data home, so the ACTIVE column holds BOTH the 2-member plan `p` and the new 0-member plan `q`, and `planCardIdx[2] = 0` lands back on `p`. Probe output: "ACTIVE column holds 2 plan(s); cursor is on plan-8a8cbbad (\"Cross-repo migration\") with 2 member(s)" and the resulting status is the `%d of %d member(s)` string - the second arm again. This is the same shape as REV-003 (a test whose comment claims coverage it does not provide), recurring in the fix for a different issue, so it is worth closing properly rather than leaving as a known-thin spot.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. (a) In TestProjectUATRefusalIsBlocked's second block, focus the 0-member plan explicitly instead of trusting index 0 - e.g. delete `p` first (`plans.Delete("app", p.ID)`) or scan `m2.planCols[2]` for the plan whose ID == q.ID and set planCardIdx[2] to that index, then assert the status contains "has no work items yet" as well as the warn level, so the arm is unambiguous. (b) Add two small assertions for the remaining sites: drive finishPlanDone through its unshipped re-guard (set pendingPlanDone, call it, assert statusLevelWarn) and drive the planAuthorLaunchedMsg headless branch (`Update(planAuthorLaunchedMsg{session: ""})`, assert statusLevelWarn and the amber marker in View()). (c) Optionally assert attachSession leaves statusLevel OK. Re-run the four reverts to confirm each now fails.
issues.fix_summary: (a) Fixed the fixture bug: TestProjectUATRefusalIsBlocked's second block now DELETES the 2-member plan first, asserts the ACTIVE column holds exactly the 0-member plan, and asserts the status contains "has no work items yet" - so the arm is unambiguous instead of silently re-testing the first. (b) Added three guards for the previously-unguarded sites: TestFinishPlanDoneRefusalIsBlocked (drives finishPlanDone through its unshipped re-guard, asserts warn + the amber marker in View() + that the plan was not flipped), TestHeadlessAnalystIsBlocked (drives Update(planAuthorLaunchedMsg{session:""}), asserts warn + the marker + that the log path and anchor note survive), and TestAttachingCueStaysOK (seeds a stale statusLevelErr and asserts the attaching cue resets it). All four reverts now fail the suite.

issues.title: docs/cli-contract.md still describes 0.28.0 as "all TUI/`launch`-side" after the REV-002 fix changed cli/plan.go
issues.description: docs/cli-contract.md:85 opens the 0.28.0 note with "Three linked fixes to the cockpit, all TUI/`launch`-side." That was accurate when it was written; after the REV-002 fix it is not - `cli/plan.go` changed, and with it the runtime behaviour of two documented commands (`gogo plan go` fans out the spawn, `gogo plan promote` spawns one source): both now fold an over-budget brief to an on-disk pointer instead of refusing. The adjacent claim "No command-surface change (the CLI enum-sync is untouched)" is still true - no verb, flag or output shape changed - so this is a description drift, not an enum-sync break. README.md's launch-diagnostics bullet (around line 505-515) has the same gap: it presents the fold as a cockpit behaviour and never says the scriptable `gogo plan` doors do it too, which is exactly the reassurance a user hitting this on the CLI needs. code-review-standards.md #1 asks that no place still describe the old behaviour.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, two sentences. (a) docs/cli-contract.md:85 - change "all TUI/`launch`-side" to "TUI-, `launch`- and `plan`-command-side" and add to the FR1 bullet: "the same fold is applied at the headless doors (`gogo plan go`, `gogo plan promote`), which build the identical intent - so the cockpit and the scriptable surface behave the same." (b) README.md's launch-diagnostics bullet - append "...and the same fold applies to `gogo plan go` / `gogo plan promote`, so the scriptable surface is not left behind." No other `docs/*.md` or skill describes this behaviour (grepped), so those two edits close it.
issues.fix_summary: Synced both sites, and corrected two further drifts of the same class found while there. docs/cli-contract.md:85 now reads "TUI-, `launch`- and `plan`-command-side", and the FR1 bullet says the same fold is applied at the headless doors (`gogo plan go`, `gogo plan promote`) which build the identical intent. README's launch-diagnostics bullet gained "...and the same fold applies to `gogo plan go` / `gogo plan promote`, so the scriptable surface is not left behind." Also corrected: both docs listed only three exact-match probes (stale after REV-008 added attach-session/switch-client) and both described capture-pane as using `-t "=<name>"` when it needs the PANE form `-t "=<name>:"` (the A2 correction had never reached the docs); and both now note the pre-0.28.0 session compatibility from REV-009.
